candidates.summary: creatingRealmPath returns rlm.Path for any package with a realm record, so a stdlib or p/ package-level object is Of-ok with an address and a PkgPath that is not a realm (Of(strings.ToUpper).PkgPath() == "strings")
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm calls reflect.Of(strings.ToUpper): ok=true, PkgPath "strings", address g1q37e4qy20davf35rwzuuu3662fnhf7f3v7npzr derived from the strings stdlib's clock. PkgPath() is documented as 'the realm that created it' and no realm owns this object; per the ADR an answer once given cannot be withdrawn ('by then that address is in a balance'), so shipping ok=true for non-realm package objects is a permanent decision the code makes silently

candidates.summary: declaredTypeName only names a pointer's pointee, so a stamped func value of a declared func type reports Type() "" and String() "<untyped>#N" although its dynamic type is the declared type
candidates.failure_scenario: type Handler func() int; var h Handler = func() int {...} persisted; reflect.Of(h) is ok=true with Type() "" and String() "<untyped>#13 (...)"; the field comment on Object.typ promises '"<pkgpath>.<Name>" of the object's declared type', and "" is also what a pointer to an anonymous struct returns, so the caller cannot tell the two apart
